mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC (from -45.1% to -37.6%, a 7.5 percentage point gain over three weeks) signals momentum in consumer mobility that will continue linearly over the next four weeks, producing net positive direction in RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 7.5 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days declines relative to the prior 28-day mean, or the week-on-week improvement reverses for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility decline from 20.1% to 18.0% (t-2w to t-0w) indicates residents are spending less time at home, implying increased outdoor and retail activity. This behavioral shift will sustain over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC higher.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 19.0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 2.1 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 20.0 in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has improved from -34.9% to -25.1% (9.8 percentage point gain), indicating outdoor recreation is recovering. This outdoor activity substitutes for retail-and-recreation visits in the short term, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks despite overall mobility recovery.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 9.8 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean, or PARKS mobility stalls or declines.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remains severely depressed at -73.0% (minimal week-on-week improvement of 1.1 points over three weeks). Persistent transit suppression constrains commuting and access to retail clusters, preventing RETAIL_REC from recovering significantly over the next four weeks despite modest retail gains.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -70.0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved only 1.4 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves by more than 5 points in a single week, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean by more than 3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near baseline (declining from -3.9% to -1.0%), indicating essential shopping is normalized. This normalization of essential mobility frees behavioral capacity for discretionary retail-and-recreation visits, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -2.0 for one week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 2.9 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM declines below -3.0 in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains suppressed at -33.0% with minimal recovery (1.9 points over three weeks), signaling continued remote-work or workplace restrictions. Persistent workplace suppression limits weekday foot traffic and commuter-driven retail spending, constraining RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -32.0 for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved only 1.9 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 points in a single week, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent improvement in RETAIL_REC (7.5 points), PARKS (9.8 points), and RESIDENTIAL decline (2.1 points) signals a regime shift toward outdoor and discretionary mobility. When all three signals align positively, RETAIL_REC will accelerate over the next two weeks as behavioral patterns stabilize in the new regime.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC and PARKS both improve >5 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL declines
evidence_refs: fact:all three series moved in expected directions from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: Any of the three series reverses direction for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not exceed the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain jointly suppressed (TRANSIT -73.0%, WORKPLACES -33.0%), indicating structural barriers to commuting. This dual suppression will persist over the next week, preventing the commuter-driven retail recovery needed to reverse RETAIL_REC's negative trajectory, keeping it below baseline.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT < -70.0 and WORKPLACES < -32.0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show minimal week-on-week improvement
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES improves by more than 4 points in the next week, or RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days exceeds the prior 7-day mean.
